result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Sparkling may assign without consent to affiliates and qualifying transaction successors; Garman requires Sparkling’s consent for any assignment, subject to a reasonableness standard, and may never assign to a Sparkling competitor. It creates no termination right tied to Sparkling’s change of control. The conforming amendment to subsection (c) is necessary to avoid conflict. Drafting is professional, though placing the Section 20(d) exception before the entire list in subsection (c) creates slight syntactic ambiguity as to whether it modifies only assignment or also transfer, lease, export and sublicensing of the Work.
